query: How does CPython intern strings so identical string literals can share the same object?

matches.reason: Core interning logic: looks up the string in the global interned hashtable and per-interpreter interned dict, and if an equal string already exists returns that shared object instead of the new one.
Promotes a mortal interned string to immortal so it remains valid as the single shared instance for the process lifetime.
Public API wrappers that the compiler and C code call to intern string literals/names, delegating to intern_common for the actual sharing logic.
Defines the per-interpreter interned dict and process-global interned hashtable that back the interning mechanism.
